To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) for the basic case of non-recycled resources, our pricing function design achieves the best worst-case social welfare performance; (2) for the more realistic case of multi-type resources with resource recycling, our pricing functions can be designed in a modular way, by applying the basic case to each type of resource.

the optimal online posted pricing functions for resource allocation in a multi-type cloud system are: 1) a linear function of the current resource utilization ratio for each resource type; and 2) a linear function in the number of time slots a job is allocated resources for.

the optimal posted prices for online cloud resource allocation are a function of the current resource utilization ratio and that the optimal pricing functions are different in the single-type and multiple-types resource cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of pricing functions for cloud resource allocation, which can be used to determine the unit price for each type of resource, based on current resource occupation ratios, to optimize social welfare.
the problem of designing optimal posted prices to maximize the provider's social welfare in cloud resource allocation.
the design and analysis of posted pricing functions for online cloud resource allocation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the competitive ratios for the proposed pricing functions in this paper are provably optimal in all considered settings, and the competitive ratios are tight in all cases.
our pricing functions are provably optimal for all possible resource demand-supply relationships, and for all possible job resource occupation durations, in terms of social welfare.
, for a cloud system with $n$ resource types, the competitive ratio of our pricing function design in terms of social welfare is $\Theta\bigl(\frac{n}{\log n}\bigr)$, which is optimal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed optimal pricing functions for online resource allocation in cloud systems, and that our pricing functions are simple and easy to implement.
we design a family of pricing functions for online cloud resource allocation that are optimal, in the sense that they achieve the smallest competitive ratio in social welfare.
the competitive ratio for a posted price-based cloud resource allocation system depends on the demand-supply relationship, the resource occupation duration, and the number of resource types.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to achieve a small worst-case competitive ratio in social welfare, the cloud provider must use a pricing scheme that is adaptive to resource utilization ratios and the number of resource types.
the cloud provider can use the utilization ratios to design optimal pricing functions that maximize social welfare.

the competitive ratios for our pricing functions are independent of the number of resource types and the number of time slots in a job, and are only a function of the resource demand and supply distributions.
